theory.intro: For multiplication and division you can choose a mental strategy or a written algorithm. Pick whichever is quicker and reliable for the numbers in front of you.
facts: **Mental** methods suit friendly numbers: doubling/halving, multiplying by $10$ or $100$, or splitting a number into parts.
Written multiplication or division methods help keep track of the working when the numbers are less friendly.
Split a number into useful parts, then combine the partial results. For example, $6\times23=6\times20+6\times3=138$.
steps: Look at the numbers and decide: are they friendly enough for a mental method?
If yes, use doubling, place value or splitting; if no, set out a written algorithm.
Estimate first so you can check your answer is sensible.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $25$ is one quarter of $100$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}28\times25\\&=28\times100\div4\\&=2800\div4\\&=700\end{aligned}$
(b) Halve $76$ and double $50$ to keep the same product.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}76\times50\\&=38\times100\\&=3800\end{aligned}$

(a) Divide by $4$ by halving twice.
$\begin{aligned}936\div2&=468\\468\div2&=234\end{aligned}$
So $936\div4=234$.
(b) Double the dividend, then divide by $10$. Both numbers have been doubled, so the quotient stays the same.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}625\div5\\&=1250\div10\\&=125\end{aligned}$

(a) Multiply both numbers by $4$ so the divisor becomes $100$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8700\div25\\&=34800\div100\\&=348\end{aligned}$
(b) Split the dividend into convenient multiples of $9$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3276\div9\\&=(3240\div9)+(36\div9)\\&=360+4\\&=364\end{aligned}$

(a) Multiply by $100$, then subtract one group of $47$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}47\times99\\&=4700-47\\&=4653\end{aligned}$
(b) Double one factor and halve the other to keep the same product.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}125\times56\\&=250\times28\\&=500\times14\\&=1000\times7\\&=7000\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Choose a reliable method and calculate.
(a) $6\times132$
(b) $286\times34$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Mental partitioning gives three simple products.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6\times132\\&=6\times100+6\times30+6\times2\\&=600+180+12\\&=792\end{aligned}$
(b) A written method keeps both partial products in place.
$\begin{aligned}286\times4&=1144\\286\times30&=8580\end{aligned}$
$\begin{array}{r}286\\\times34\\\hline1144\\8580\\\hline9724\end{array}$
So $286\times34=9724$.
An estimate $300\times30=9000$ confirms the size is sensible.

workedExamples.question_text: Choose an efficient mental strategy and calculate $83\times10$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiplying by $10$ makes each digit worth ten times as much.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}83\times10\\&=830\end{aligned}$

(a) Use $100$ groups of $75$, then subtract the six extra groups.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}94\times75\\&=(100\times75)-(6\times75)\\&=7500-450\\&=7050\end{aligned}$
(b) Use $4000$ groups of $25$, then subtract the eight extra groups. Multiplying by $25$ is multiplying by $100$, then dividing by $4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3992\times25\\&=(4000\times25)-(8\times25)\\&=(4000\times100\div4)-(8\times100\div4)\\&=100000-200\\&=99800\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: Choose an efficient mental strategy and calculate $46 \times 10$.
foundation.solution_text:
Multiplying by $10$ shifts each digit one place left.
$46 \times 10$
$=460$

Decide whether a mental or written method is more reliable for $347 \times 26$, then calculate.
foundation.solution_text:
The factors are not friendly, so a written method is reliable.
$347 \times 6=2082$
$347 \times 20=6940$
$2082+6940$
$=9022$

development.question_text: Use doubling and halving to calculate $125 \times 48$ mentally.
Use a place-value shortcut to calculate $735 \div 5$ mentally.
development.solution_text:
Double both the dividend and divisor so the divisor becomes $10$.
$735\div5=1470\div10$
$=147$

development.question_text: Use convenient factors to calculate $4\,608 \div 16$ mentally.

Calculate $4\,136 \times 37$.
Explain why a written method is appropriate.
development.solution_text:
Neither factor is friendly, so a written method reduces the risk of losing a part-product.
$4\,136 \times 7=28\,952$
$4\,136 \times 30=124\,080$
$28\,952+124\,080$
$=153\,032$
